$comment: ADR-037 register fragment (connectors-webshop-orders). The dormant WooCommerce shop template, its mapping onto shillinq's WebshopOrder and an incremental synchronization of the shop's orders. No code: the synchronization engine does the work.

objects.name: WooCommerce shop
objects.description: A WooCommerce web shop (WooCommerce REST API v3, https://woocommerce.github.io/woocommerce-rest-api-docs/). Orders: GET <shop>/wp-json/wc/v3/orders, paged by `page` and `per_page` (at most 100), changed-since filter `modified_after`. Auth: a REST API consumer key and secret over HTTP Basic, the secret held by the credential broker. Set the location to your shop's address followed by /wp-json/wc/v3, the consumer key, and the credential, then enable.

objects.name: WooCommerce order to shillinq WebshopOrder
objects.description: One WooCommerce order as shillinq's WebshopOrder (shillinq sales-webshop-orders, design D2). Fill `channelId` and `administrationId` with the ids of this shop's WebshopChannel in shillinq (Sales, Web shops): the synchronization does not run while either is empty. The mapping never writes shillinq's own fields (`intakeState`, `arInvoiceId`, `creditNoteId`, `refusalReason`). `payment.status` is paid, pending, refunded or cancelled; a later fetch of the same order updates it on the same object.

mapping.buyer.name: {{ (billing.first_name|default('') ~ ' ' ~ billing.last_name|default(''))|trim }}
mapping.buyer.address: {{ ([billing.address_1|default(''), billing.address_2|default(''), (billing.postcode|default('') ~ ' ' ~ billing.city|default(''))|trim]|filter(p => p is not empty))|join(', ') }}
mapping.lines: {{ line_items|map(l => {sku: l.sku|default(''), description: l.name, quantity: l.quantity, unitPrice: (l.quantity > 0 ? ((prices_include_tax ? l.total + l.total_tax : l.total) / l.quantity) : 0)|round(2), vatRate: (l.total > 0 ? (l.total_tax / l.total * 100) : 0)|round(0)})|json_encode }}

objects.name: WooCommerce orders to shillinq
objects.description: Writes the WooCommerce shop's orders into shillinq as one WebshopOrder each, incrementally: each run asks only for orders changed since the last complete run (`modified_after`, read from each order's `date_modified_gmt`), and the cursor moves only after a complete fetch. Each order is kept on its shop order id, so a later refund or cancellation updates the payment status of the WebshopOrder already written and never makes a second one. Nothing is deleted. Off until the source and the mapping's channel and administration ids are filled.

requiredMappingValues.name: the shillinq WebshopChannel id of this WooCommerce shop
the shillinq administration id of this WooCommerce shop
